- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.3) within 5 days, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to counteract downward bias.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–14 day horizons; if forecast is > 2σ above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–3%.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 5 days show strong upward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive rising prices), model often fails to capture exhaustion; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals (e.g., +1, -1, +1), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction 1–2 days ahead.
